patch_description: The key insight from the prior programs: basin quality is the binding constraint, and random single-point perturbations waste most evaluations. The novel approach here replaces blind stochastic moves with *exact gradient information from the bottleneck triangle itself*: the area of the smallest triangle is a simple quadratic function of its three vertices, so its gradient (perpendicular push away from the opposite edge for each vertex) is computable in closed form. I implement (1) a fast incremental evaluator that recomputes only the 66 affected triangles when a single point moves, (2) a deterministic gradient-ascent mode that simultaneously translates all three bottleneck vertices along their exact area gradients with adaptive step size (a correlated move random noise cannot discover), and (3) basin-hopping kicks that, per the recommendation, perturb only 3–4 vertices at σ=0.13–0.15 or rigidly translate the bottleneck triangle, followed by a quick gradient-polish. Scale-invariance is handled by rescaling to unit hull area after each accepted move, keeping the score well-conditioned.
